Threads of the BLAS Library

Source: R/utils.r
blas_threads.Rd

Get or set how many threads R's BLAS/LAPACK library uses, while R is running.

Usage

blas_threads(n = NULL)

Arguments

n

NULL to only read the count, or a whole number of at least 1 to set it to. Any other value sets nothing.

Value

The thread count before the call: an integer of at least 1, or NA when it can't be read. Invisibly when n is given.

Details

R computes matrix operations such as %*%, crossprod(), solve(), eigen(), and cmdscale() with the BLAS/LAPACK library it is linked to. Optimized libraries run each large operation on several threads. Environment variables such as OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS set how many before the library loads; blas_threads() changes it afterward.

The count can be read and set with OpenBLAS, Intel MKL, BLIS, and FlexiBLAS (which passes it on to its backend). It can't with R's reference BLAS (which is single-threaded), Apple's Accelerate, or any other library: there blas_threads() returns NA and setting does nothing. It never raises an error, warning, or message.

Setting is limited to what is known to be safe. The count is only read, not set:

  • With OpenBLAS's OpenMP builds before version 0.3.34, which take their count from OpenMP's, and OpenBLAS builds that don't report whether they use OpenMP, such as Ubuntu 20.04's.

  • With FlexiBLAS, unless its backend is OpenBLAS (but not an OpenMP build), BLIS, or MKL, and only while that backend is in use.

  • In a process forked from the one that loaded ecodive, e.g. by parallel::mclapply().

Otherwise, the count can be lowered and raised again, but not above the highest count read from the library, so that it never has to start threads it didn't already have: a larger n is reduced to that. When no count was read, only n = 1 is set. OpenMP's thread count is left as it is.

On Windows, the library is the one in Rblas.dll and Rlapack.dll, which can be replaced with copies of an optimized library. If both are, each copy has a count of its own: both are set, and the larger is returned.

ecodive's own functions don't use the BLAS; their threads are set by cpus.

See also

n_cpus()

Examples

    blas_threads()
#> [1] 4

    # Use one thread for a matrix product, then restore the count.
    # Restoring NA (count unknown) sets nothing.
    old <- blas_threads(1)
    x   <- crossprod(matrix(runif(1e4), 100))
    blas_threads(old)
